nodes.label: React (Frontend Tech)
nodes.rationale: Project explicitly restricted to React frontend conventions; instructions state this overrides default behavior and Node.js/npm-based build tooling must not be introduced.

nodes.label: PHP (Backend Tech)
nodes.rationale: Backend restricted to PHP conventions; Python scripts/tooling must not be introduced anywhere in the project.

nodes.label: Sequential Batch Build Order
nodes.rationale: Full scope broken into sequential, buildable batches where each batch only depends on the ones before it, so they can be developed and tested in order.

nodes.label: Development Notes (No Python/Node, No Caching, Single Admin)
nodes.norm_label: development notes (no python/node, no caching, single admin)

nodes.label: Single-Admin, No-Login Access Model
nodes.rationale: Keeps the app simple: single admin user, no authentication/login layer required at any point in the design.

nodes.label: Comments Feature (Live YouTube Fetch, AI-Suggested Replies)
nodes.norm_label: comments feature (live youtube fetch, ai-suggested replies)

nodes.label: Video Status Workflow (draft→prepared→scheduled→published/failed)
nodes.rationale: draft can only advance to prepared once every required field (title, description, tags, thumbnail_ref, video_type, video_path) is validly filled in, ensuring nothing incomplete gets scheduled.

nodes.label: Out of Scope Constraints
nodes.rationale: Python and Node.js are excluded entirely, no login/auth system, no platforms beyond YouTube, and no local comments/analytics tables — keeps the app deliberately minimal and always-live.

nodes.label: Frontend-Backend REST Boundary Principle
nodes.rationale: Every feature is backed by a REST API endpoint; the React frontend never talks to the database directly, always going through the PHP REST API — enforces a single source of truth in the backend.

nodes.label: Buildless React + Plain PHP Stack
nodes.rationale: React is buildless (in-browser Babel, vendored locally, no npm/Node) and PHP is plain with no framework — chosen so the project never needs Python or Node.js/npm tooling.

nodes.label: backend/.env Wiring Target
nodes.rationale: Nothing here is committed to git — backend/.env is gitignored and per-account secrets go straight into the database, keeping credentials out of version control.
